ox.service.showPage.description:
Show a web action's existing live page: `await ox.service.showPage({ purpose, name, input?, session?, pageUrl?, waitForUserInteraction? })`. Pass the original qualified action name, input, and routing, preserving omitted fields; session and pageUrl may coexist. Uses the latest matching invocation's actual page and defaulted session, without discovery, invocation, navigation, reload, submission, or replacement. Fails if the page was reused, closed, busy, unavailable, or cannot be presented; never replay a mutation to obtain it.

Use this for service drafts, review, human verification, and payment, not Browser's showPage or an ordinary URL link. Prepare the visible page through ordinary actions; preparation must not submit orders or payment. Login uses the website's standard login action.

By default returns immediately: iOS adds a live-page card expandable only by the user; macOS opens a Host window. iOS keeps the latest page inline per conversation when returning from navigation or backgrounding and after Done/Cancel. Reopened cards show live state, not snapshots. When the user must complete a step, explain it and set waitForUserInteraction: true to show Done/Cancel and suspend this call until the user chooses. Returns completion only in this mode: "completed" when the user taps Done, or "cancelled" when the user taps Cancel or closes the page. On cancellation, stop dependent work and do not reopen automatically. Done acknowledges interaction, not successful verification or payment; inspect fresh state before resuming and never automatically repeat writes. Without waiting, explain the step and end the turn; do not poll or continue dependent work. Presentation proves neither interaction nor completion.

name.description: The same qualified web action name used for the page's invocation.

input.description: The same action input, used only to select its execution page.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

waitForUserInteraction.description: Show Done/Cancel and wait for the user. completion is completed when the user taps Done and cancelled when the user taps Cancel or closes the page. Defaults to false.

ox.service.attach.description: Attach a service by domain: `await ox.service.attach({ purpose, domain })`. Exact IDs take precedence; a unique web/API domain match also accepts www., case, trailing-dot, and URL variants. Results use the canonical service domain; use that returned domain for subsequent calls. On a miss or ambiguity, use ox.service.find with the service name or task and attach an exact returned domain before concluding support is missing. First use saves and attaches it; later calls reload this conversation's attachment from current source. Source edits alone do not reload. For ordinary use, attach then inspect needed contracts in one execution; read source only for authoring, repair, comparison, or deletion. First attachment is allowed by default but honors configured Action policies; denied approval throws and must not be retried blindly. Attachment does not check access, discover sessions, or start login. Returns a snapshot with reloaded; access and handoffs use standard service actions.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.create.description: Save a remote MCP connection with `{ purpose, kind: "mcp", name, endpoint, transport?, faviconUrl? }`. Choose an explicit display name from the product name or user request; never derive it from the endpoint hostname or use the MCP server-reported name. faviconUrl is an optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL; anonymous loading permits up to five public HTTPS redirects. MCP saves the connection to the Local repository at `repositories/local/mcp/<domain>/service.json` without connecting or requesting login; it returns the assigned domain, derived from the endpoint host, for inspect/attach/invoke/delete. Discover non-standard tools explicitly with inspect and invoke the server's standard authorize action if authorization is required. An existing endpoint is reused; use update to change its settings or refresh tools. MCP connections save immediately. Never put credentials in the endpoint; invoke authorize. This connects to a server, not hosts one. Create web/API source directly with ox.fs under repositories/local/<kind>/<id>/ and register its <kind>:<id> in repositories/local/repository.json services before validation and attachment.

endpoint.description: Public HTTPS MCP endpoint without credentials. Required for MCP; omit domain.

faviconUrl.description: Optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL for this MCP connection.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

name.description: Explicit service display name chosen from the product name or user request; do not derive it from the endpoint hostname.

ox.service.delete.description: Delete a Local web service or remove an MCP connection: `await ox.service.delete({ purpose, domain })`. The user approves deletion. Inspect the target source before deleting it and preserve unrelated work. For web services, source deletion is immediate and another repository candidate may become active. There is no built-in version history to restore deleted source. MCP removal is immediate, deletes a Local definition, detaches it from this conversation, clears local authorization and tool approvals, and does not revoke access at the server or delete a non-Local repository definition.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.detach.description: Detach a service (by domain) from this conversation: `await ox.service.detach({ purpose, domain })`. Removes it from the conversation's attachment bar so its actions stop being available; the service stays saved. Use when the user is done with it or you attached the wrong one. Returns the service snapshot (`attached: false`). `purpose` is a short (<10 words) human-readable description shown to the user as the step label.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.inspect.description: Inspect service actions: `await ox.service.inspect({ purpose, domain, cursor? })`. Returns service metadata, available standard action IDs, and up to ten complete non-standard action input/output contracts ordered by action ID. Pass nextCursor unchanged to continue; its absence marks the last page. Never infer that an action is absent until needed pages are read. Reuse returned contracts without inspecting again; fetch another page only when needed, or batch bounded pagination when all actions are required. Standard action contracts are supplied upfront and are not repeated here. Optional website actions are available only when listed in standardActions; incompatible same-named custom actions remain in actions with their own contracts. Capability discovery failure throws rather than returning an empty successful page. Human verification and payment use ordinary preparation actions followed by ox.service.showPage.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

additionalProperties.description: Complete action inputSchema and outputSchema with metadata.

standardActions.description: Available standard action IDs; their contracts are supplied upfront.

nextCursor.description: Continuation cursor; absent after the last page.

ox.service.invoke.description:
Invoke a service action: `await ox.service.invoke({ purpose, name, input?, session?, pageUrl? })`. Names use web:<domain>:<action>, api:<service>:<action>, ios:<app>:<action>, or mcp:<server>:<action>. Use supplied standard contracts or complete contracts from ox.service.inspect without rediscovering them. Runtime approvals are authoritative; never invent approval fields or repeat denied calls.

For session-aware websites, omitted session discovers fresh accounts and defaults to the first descriptor, for public and protected actions, including when pageUrl routes discovery. Discovery/login actions never auto-select. Without sessions, public actions remain public and protected actions fail before dispatch. To honor an intended account/tenant or consequential target, invoke listSessions and pass a real descriptor explicitly; never fabricate one. The Host revalidates it on the selected page and fails stale selections without switching accounts. Reuse it for account-stable work; do not preflight every action. Handlers receive context.session and must verify the actual account/tenant.

session selects account/context; its url is validated context metadata, not a navigation override. Execution uses the action baseUrl, inherited from the service when omitted, with declared input parameters resolved. Optional pageUrl overrides that destination with a public HTTPS target within the service domain, not account selection. Both may be supplied. Website conversation continuations retain their initial account and target. Invoke standard login for authentication; acknowledgment, cached login fields, and descriptors alone are not proof of current access.

Failed calls may have effects: inspect state before retrying writes. Cross-check empty, partial, or implausible results before reporting absence. Read Evolve to build or repair missing/defective web or API actions, then invoke them; Browser is not a fulfillment fallback. MCP and iOS implementations are not editable; report concrete blockers.

input.description: Input matching the upfront standard contract or the non-standard contract from ox.service.inspect.

pageUrl.description: Optional execution URL override within the service domain. Otherwise use the input-resolved action/service baseUrl, not session.url.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

outputSchema.description: The action's output, defined by its upfront standard contract or inspected non-standard contract.

ox.service.list.description: List the selected service sources from enabled repositories: `await ox.service.list({ purpose, kind? })`. Filter by web, api, ios, or mcp. Includes unattached services and invalid web/API definitions with repository, manifestPath, and validationError so they can be repaired. Listing does not attach, load website pages, check access, or discover MCP tools. Absence of validationError is not proof that handlers or live actions work; validate Local drafts explicitly. Use this for inventory and repair, not as a ceiling on website access. Choose research domains from the request; build missing actions through Evolve. Use listAttached for this conversation's attachments.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.listAttached.description: List this conversation's attached services, not the domains Ox can access: `await ox.service.listAttached({ purpose, kind? })`. Filter by `kind: "web"` for website services, `kind: "api"` for HTTP API services, `kind: "ios"` for device services, or `kind: "mcp"` for remote MCP servers. Every result includes its kind.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.update.description:
Update an existing service by domain: `await ox.service.update({ purpose, domain, ...fields })`. Supported fields depend on the existing service kind; unsupported fields are rejected, and omitted fields are preserved. This never creates a missing service or changes its kind. All service kinds and repository sources support name as a local display-name override, applied immediately and preserved across restarts and source refreshes. Renaming leaves service identity, action names, source manifests, connections, and authorization unchanged.

Web, API, and native services support only name through this function. Edit Local web/API manifests and actions.js with ox.fs under repositories/local/. Register new sources in repositories/local/repository.json, validate the draft, resolve a source conflict explicitly when needed, then attach to load/reload. Credentials never belong in source.

Local MCP connections additionally support endpoint, transport, and faviconUrl. MCP also accepts a connection name or unique endpoint host as domain. With no fields, reconnects and refreshes tools; a name-only update does not reconnect. Set transport to auto for detection. Set faviconUrl to a public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL, or null to restore server-advertised icons. Explicit icons load anonymously with up to five public HTTPS redirects; server-advertised icons remain same-site without redirects. Connection changes validate before replacing and save immediately; failure preserves the old connection. Changing endpoint keeps the domain but clears old local authorization and tool approvals. Tool contracts and implementation belong to the server and cannot be edited here. Other repositories' MCP connection settings are read-only; copy them to Local before changing connection settings.

domain.description: Existing service domain. Direct MCP also accepts a saved connection name or unique endpoint host.

faviconUrl.description: Public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL for a Local MCP connection; null restores MCP-advertised icons.

name.description: Local display name for any service kind.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.validate.description: Validate a complete Local web or API service draft: `await ox.service.validate({ purpose, domain })`. Checks the manifest, action installer and matching action IDs, required files, and service size limits together. Reusable skills are independent packages verified through evolve. Returns `{ domain, valid: true }` or throws with the validation error. Does not edit, attach, reload, Save, or invoke service actions. Finish related source edits before calling; individual file writes do not validate service contents.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.
